page: Microsoft Azure E2bs_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EBSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no local storage or GPU bundled with this instance, but it is Premium Storage capable to support external block storage.

Benchmark data reveals a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, register in the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read and write speeds categorized as poor at 15.07 GB/sec and 13.81 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and Redis SET performance are similarly constrained, with Redis achieving 1.98 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2bs_v5 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio within a low-vCPU footprint, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense parallel processing. Given the poor multi-core and database benchmark results, it is less suited for heavy database engines or high-throughput web serving. Instead, it is appropriate for lightweight memory-intensive tasks, basic text processing, single-threaded compression utilities, or small-scale development environments requiring Premium Storage capabilities.
